text:
Alex: Hey team — ACME POC reports their free credits dropped ~35% overnight. They swear they only ran a few short embedding jobs. Can we triage?
Maya: @Alex can you paste the customer request id / sample call?
Alex: They sent this snippet: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test..." \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":["doc1","doc2"]}'
```
Alex: They said each doc ~300 tokens, only 2 docs but console shows 120k tokens billed.
Sam: That smells like accidental loop/retries or streaming vs non-streaming counting. Any retry headers?
Irene: Also which SDK version? older SDKs didn't set idempotency by default on retries.
Alex: Customer using our python sdk v0.8.1.
Jordan: BillingBot shows a usage spike around 02:14 UTC: "embeddings_units: 4, tokens_in: 120480" (estimate). Could that be multiple background jobs?
BillingBot: [auto] Quick ledger: account acme-poc — estimated tokens: 120480, embeddings units: 4, credits used: 0.37. Invoice link: https://billing.redwood/inv/xyz
Priya: Can we get request logs from the runtime for that window? run `rg 02:14` in the runtime logs.
Sam: Also check for streaming=true in the request body — streaming can cause token echoing when clients don't consume and reconnect.
Irene: Another vector: they were using the bulk endpoint without batching limits; if client retried per-item we might multiply tokens.
Alex: Pasted a small runtime excerpt from customer-provided logs:
```
[02:14:03] req_id=abc123 model=embed-large input_count=2 tokens=600
[02:14:03] req_id=abc123 -> error ECONNRESET retry
[02:14:04] req_id=abc123 retry=1 model=embed-large input_count=2 tokens=600
[02:14:05] req_id=abc123 retry=2 model=embed-large input_count=2 tokens=600
```
Maya: That clearly shows 3 attempts for same payload — that's ~1800 tokens but still far from 120k.
Sam: Multiplication factor still off. Could client have looped over a larger doc set and only sent sample to us?
Jordan: Check for background crawler: I see repeated 10k-token requests earlier from same API key at 01:50 UTC. different req_ids but same key.
Alex: I asked customer — they have a loop in their data prep that mistakenly expanded a short doc into tokenized chunks. They only saw sample but actually ran a 10k-token batch job.
Priya: So root cause = customer workload mismatch + retries amplified by SDK version.
Irene: Action items: 1) offer one-time credit for unexpected free credits consumption, 2) recommend upgrade to SDK v0.9.3 which sets idempotency-key and reduces retry duplication, 3) suggest rate limits / quotas for POC.
Maya: I can patch account now — suggest crediting back 0.30 credits and adding a soft quota of 50k tokens for next 48h. OK?
Alex: Customer replied :thumbsup: Appreciate that. Please also send them a minimal best-practices note on bulk embeddings and idempotency keys.
Sam: I'll write the short note and add to the shared POC checklist.
BillingBot: [auto] Credit applied: 0.30 to acme-poc by Maya at 2025-11-17T02:45:00Z. Quota set: 50,000 tokens/day for 48h.
Priya: Marking resolved — customer accepted credits and updated their job to avoid the expansion bug.
Alex: Thanks all. Closing thread unless anything else.
